verdictSummary: The private core is a weekend build: journal entries, mood check-ins, reflection prompts and a local garden of original creatures are straightforward to model. Matching Voidpet Garden means more than reproducing that loop: the polished mobile experience, original creature universe, curated mental-health content and accumulated collection are real gaps. Build the personal version, but do not pretend it has Voidpet's art, writing, store distribution or ongoing content pipeline.
coreLoopDIY: Log a mood and reflection locally, grow an original creature garden from the entries, review patterns over time and export the journal whenever you want.
requirements: iOS or Android device or emulator
original creature illustrations or simple vector shapes
whatYouLose: Voidpet's original creature art, animations, names and worldbuilding
the polished native mobile experience and app-store distribution
the curated prompt, exercise, affirmation and meditation library
the accumulated collection, journal history and ongoing content updates
Giga perks such as cosmetics, larger pet limits and team templates
moatNotes: original creature IP, mobile product polish and accumulated journal and collection history
whyPeopleStillPay: People pay because the journal is only one layer of Voidpet Garden. The finished product combines a distinct creature universe, a curated set of reflective exercises, polished mobile interactions and a collection habit that becomes more valuable as entries and pets accumulate. A local clone can reproduce the data model and the loop, but not the original art, writing, updates or the work of maintaining a finished mental-health product.

notes: The honest substitute is a private mood journal with an original garden, not a copy of Voidpet's art or mental-health claims.
prompt:
Build me a private mobile mood journal with a creature garden to replace Voidpet Garden. Requirements:

- Use React Native with Expo, TypeScript, Expo Router and expo-sqlite; do not offer alternative stacks.
- The check-in screen lets me choose one of 12 emotion names, set intensity from 1 to 5, answer an original reflection prompt and save the entry locally.
- Turn each logged emotion into an original abstract creature or plant made from local SVG or vector shapes; entries grow the garden and unlock simple stages.
  Do not copy Voidpet names, art, characters or text.
- Add Garden, Check-in, History and Settings screens. History shows a 7-day mood timeline,
  emotion filters and an editable entry detail view.
- Seed 20 neutral prompts across gratitude, goals, emotional naming, relationships, body awareness
  and coping; label them as reflections, not therapy or medical advice.
- Store entries, creatures, prompt completions and settings in SQLite; add JSON export and a Delete all data action.
- Work fully offline with no accounts, telemetry, cloud sync or API keys. Keep all assets local.
- Include accessible labels, large touch targets, reduced-motion handling, empty states, validation
  and a first-run privacy note saying the app is not medical care.
- Out of scope: social features, clinical assessment, AI advice, subscriptions, notifications and App Store or Play Store release configuration.
- Include a README with setup commands, Expo permissions, the data model, export and backup instructions and the limits of using this as a personal reflective tool.
